summary: Wrote docs/plans/2026-10-25-L2-run-services.md: svc scope in run_init (stop first), services_down/SVC_UP, the trap (session scope too), six stop points, suite observation per stop point, gc's unit match rule and status lines. Captured 4 real fixtures. An Opus review found 1 Critical and 4 Important plan bugs; all fixed in the plan. Tests 270 → 270.
verified_how: check.sh: green in 454 s, 270/270; fixtures captured from real 64M harness-test-<pid>-cur/-dup scopes, each stopped; list-units 'harness-test-*' printed nothing afterwards; bash TERM probe: EXIT trap ran in 13 ms, child lived on

dead_ends.tried: stub-systemd-run recording the command pid in <unit>.pids
dead_ends.why: pids count in the stub's TasksCurrent, so every clean session would 'leave 1 process'; plan uses <unit>.cmd plus a tree kill

dead_ends.tried: INIT_CMD for check 6.9 in the user config
dead_ends.why: the project's .harness/config.sh is sourced after it and wins (lib/config.sh:31); use a dproj project

discoveries.text: Bash runs the EXIT trap at once on SIGTERM while a foreground child runs, and the child lives on: a TERM to the driver mid-session leaves claude running in harness-<run>-s<n>. Plan §4: the trap stops S_UNIT first, then services_down.
A SIGKILLed driver leaves no `ended` (the driver removes it at start; only finish and the trap write it), so gc stops units of runs with no live driver.pid, ended or not (plan §7.1).

systemd-run with a unit name still loaded exits 1: 'Failed to start transient scope unit: Unit <u>.scope was already loaded or has a fragment file.' (fixtures/systemd-run-unit-exists.txt). run_init must stop the old svc scope first.

verify() runs run_init before its mem_gate, so a memory wait leaves the verify without services: L2-04 makes it `mem_gate || run_init`. bin/harness is set -euo pipefail: TEARDOWN_CMD's default line and cmd_status's systemctl calls must always succeed (plan §2, §7.2).

questions: D2 default: the driver's EXIT trap also stops the running session's scope, not only the services. OK?
gc stops a run's units when its driver is dead even without `ended` (a SIGKILL writes none), not only for ended runs as the spec says. OK?
proposed_changes: L2-03 step 3: one marker per why (teardown-done.marker), and the order is read from systemd.log (the teardown logs a record there), not from the marker's mtime
L2-03 step 4: the TERM goes to driver.pid (--foreground runs the driver as a child of bin/harness); the trap also stops the session's scope
L2-04 step 2: the stub sets PAUSE ($STATE/PAUSE) and the suite resumes with harness resume (no session runs during a pause); the pause branch commits its note
L2-05 step 1: units qualify with no live driver.pid, `ended` or not; gc prints its own `+ stopped <unit> (<run> ended|: driver gone)` lines rather than act's raw argv
